Its first founders were Nashr Fadl Al-Sayrafi and the Al-Gharabi building in Bani Ubaidan. The first pharmacy there was owned by Dr. Abdulmajid Al-Sharabi and Dr. Abdu Amin. Among the founders of the Al-Suwaida market were Sheikh Muhammad Nasser and his son, Sheikh Ramzi Muhammad Nasser (the current market administrator). The first gas shop was owned by Ahmed Qaed Al-Muhajiri, and it still exists today.

It is now considered one of the largest and most diverse commercial markets and a major commercial hub in the Mawiyah district. Land prices in this market are among the highest in the governorate. The price per cubic meter (not the qasaba, as measurement is by the cubit) has reached 600,000 to 800,000 Yemeni rials for a single cubit on the main street. Shop rents range from 50,000 to 90,000 Yemeni rials.
